title: Compact JSON parameter schema (compatibility-first) and structured validation errors
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: We currently accept two divergent parameter shapes for tool/function calls: a verbose JSON Schema style (full JSON Schema draft subsets) and a legacy positional args array. This causes brittle validation, inconsistent error messages, and complexity in the runtime compatibility layer. Problem: teams building SDKs and runtimes need a single, compact schema dialect that is easy to author, easy to validate at runtime, and supports graceful backward compatibility with positional and older shapes.
proposal: Introduce a compact JSON parameter schema dialect (CJS-D) that maps to a constrained JSON Schema subset plus ergonomic shorthand. Implement deterministic validation with rich, machine-readable error codes and a compatibility shim that accepts legacy positional parameters and legacy "args" arrays. Validation will run in three phases: coercion/normalization, schema validation, and semantic checks (e.g., cross-field constraints). The runtime will emit structured errors with an error_code, field_path, human_message, and suggested_fix (as strings).
spec_examples: Validation error example (stringified JSON emitted by runtime): {"error_code":"ERR_REQUIRED_MISSING", "field_path":"params.user_id", "human_message":"Missing required parameter 'user_id'.", "suggested_fix":"Provide 'user_id' in named params or migrate your positional args to named params. See docs://schemas/migration"}
validation_flow: 1) Normalize incoming call: if 'args' present map to named params using the most recent positional map for the function name. 2) Coerce simple types (string->int only when safe) per explicit coercion rules. 3) Run schema validation against CJS-D. 4) Run semantic checks (e.g., if start_date > end_date error). 5) Return either success with normalized params or structured error. All phases must be deterministic and idempotent across retries.
error_codes: ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH - value type does not match schema
ERR_ENUM_VIOLATION - value not in allowed enum
ERR_PARSE_FAILURE - value could not be parsed (e.g., invalid JSON in string)
ERR_UNEXPECTED_FIELD - client passed unknown parameter not allowed by schema
ERR_DEPRECATION_WARNING - parameter used is deprecated but accepted
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement CJS-D parser and runtime validator behind feature flag; internal SDKs (JS, Python) added to opt-in. Phase 2 (6 weeks): Enable compatibility shim that maps legacy positional args to named params, emit ERR_DEPRECATION_WARNING for positional usage. Phase 3 (3 months): Start warning-only deprecation for server logs and admin console; outreach to top customers. Phase 4 (6 months): Enforce named params-only for new function definitions; existing functions get compatibility mode for 12 months. Provide migration script and example PRs in SDK repos.
acceptance_criteria: C1: Runtime accepts compact schema and validates named params according to CJS-D
C2: Compatibility shim correctly maps positional args for top-50 internal functions and emits deprecation warnings
C3: Errors are emitted with stable error_code values and documented message templates
C4: SDKs (node/python) provide helper to convert legacy args to named params and surface structured errors
C5: Tests covering coercion edge cases, enum failures, nested object validation, and compatibility scenarios in CI

notes: Decision: Use a single schema_version string embedded in the function manifest to allow runtime negotiation.
Trade-off: Compact shorthand is easier to author but requires robust parsing; we will keep longform round-tripped for storage to avoid fidelity loss.
Open question: Should enum validation be case-sensitive by default? Proposal: keep case-sensitive, offer 'ignore_case' hint in schema when desired.
Performance: aim for sub-ms additional validation overhead for the common small schemas; measure during alpha rollout.
